# ChargebackLens — Data Description Document

**Companion to:** `chargebacklens_lld.md`
**Purpose:** This is the precise contract for the five pre-generated CSVs — exact row counts, foreign-key rules, and every intentional inconsistency the dataset contains. Nothing here is generated by the notebook; this document specifies what the notebook's `validate_schema` and cleaning logic (LLD §4.1) must detect and handle. Treat every count below as a target to hit exactly during generation and a target to detect exactly during validation — if the notebook's validation logging doesn't reproduce these numbers, either the generator or the validator has a bug.

**Snapshot date:** 2026-11-01 (the date `account_age_days`, `prior_disputes`, etc. in `customers.csv` are computed as-of)
**Transaction window:** 2026-01-01 to 2026-10-31 (10 months)

---

## 1. Row count summary

| Table | Total rows | Clean rows | Rows with an injected data-quality issue | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `transactions.csv` | 120,000 | 119,528 | 472 | see §3.1 |
| `customers.csv` | 35,000 | 34,929 | 71 | see §3.2 |
| `merchants.csv` | 60 | 57 | 3 | see §3.3 |
| `fulfilment.csv` | 66,140 | 65,000 | 1,140 | see §3.4 |
| `disputes.csv` | 1,091 | 1,044 | 47 | see §3.5 |

"Rows with an injected issue" counts a row once even if it triggers more than one condition — the per-issue breakdowns in §3 will not sum exactly to this column for that reason, and each breakdown says so explicitly where it applies.

---

## 2. Foreign key specification

| Child table.column | Parent table.column | Cardinality | Enforced? | Violating rows (intentional) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `transactions.merchant_id` | `merchants.merchant_id` | many-to-one | Yes — zero violations | 0 |
| `transactions.customer_id` | `customers.customer_id` | many-to-one | Yes — zero violations | 0 |
| `fulfilment.payment_id` | `transactions.payment_id` | one-to-one (intended) | **No — 140 orphan rows** | 140 |
| `disputes.payment_id` | `transactions.payment_id` | one-to-one (intended, "at most once") | **No — 35 orphan rows, 6 duplicate rows** | 41 |

Rationale for the two unenforced FKs: `fulfilment.csv` and `disputes.csv` are the two tables most plausibly produced by a *different upstream system* than `transactions.csv` (a logistics partner feed and a bank/network dispute feed, respectively) in a real payments stack. ID mismatches between systems that were never reconciled are the single most common real-world data-quality problem in exactly this kind of join, so the dataset reproduces it deliberately rather than assuming a clean join. `merchant_id` and `customer_id` are first-party fields written by the same system that writes `transactions.csv`, so those two are kept clean — an unenforced violation there wouldn't be realistic, it would just be a bug.

**Directive to `validate_schema` (LLD §4.1):** referential integrity checks on `merchant_id`/`customer_id` should raise (`AssertionError`) on any violation, because none are expected. Checks on `fulfilment.payment_id` and `disputes.payment_id` should **log and drop** orphan rows rather than raise, and the logged count should be asserted to equal the numbers in this document (140 and 35 respectively) as a regression check that the loader isn't silently dropping more or fewer rows than intended.

---

## 3. Per-table specification

### 3.1 `transactions.csv` — 120,000 rows

**Grain:** one row per payment attempt. **Primary key:** `payment_id`, intended unique.

| Column | Dtype | Null count | Value domain |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `payment_id` | string | 0 | unique per §3.1.1 below |
| `merchant_id` | string | 0 | one of 60 values in `merchants.csv` |
| `customer_id` | string | 0 | one of 35,000 values in `customers.csv` |
| `amount` | float64 | 0 | > 0, except §3.1.4 |
| `method` | category | 0 | `upi` (44%), `card` (31%), `netbanking` (12%), `wallet` (9%), `emi` (4%) |
| `issuer_bank` | string | 62,400 (52%) | null for all `upi`/`wallet` rows by design (not a data-quality issue — a structural null) |
| `card_bin_country` | string | 82,800 (69%) | null for all non-`card` rows by design (structural null) |
| `created_at` | datetime64 | 0 | 2026-01-01 to 2026-10-31, except §3.1.5 |
| `ip_state` | string | 0 | Indian state code, except §3.1.2 |
| `device_id` | string | 0 | except §3.1.3 |
| `is_first_txn_for_device` | bool | 0 | |
| `checkout_latency_ms` | int64 | 0 | typically 800–15,000, except §3.1.6 |
| `retry_count` | int64 | 0 | typically 0–4, except §3.1.7 |
| `auth_status` | category | 0 | always `success` (only successful auths are in scope) |

**Merchant-category volume split** (drives §3.3 and §3.4 sizing): `d2c` 42,000 · `gaming` 24,000 · `subscription` 18,000 · `travel` 12,000 · `edtech` 12,000 · `ticketing` 12,000.

#### Injected issues in `transactions.csv`

1. **§3.1.1 — Duplicate `payment_id`:** 12 payment_ids each appear on 2 rows (24 rows total), with a differing `amount` or `checkout_latency_ms` between the pair, simulating a retry that was double-written to the export. Unique payment_ids: 119,988 across 120,000 rows. **Tests:** the "no payment_id appears twice" assertion in `build_label` (LLD §4.1) — this is the exact condition that assertion exists to catch, so the generator must produce it and the assertion must fire on it before any deduplication step.
2. **§3.1.2 — Inconsistent `ip_state` casing/format:** 360 rows (0.30%) use a non-standard representation of an otherwise valid state — mixed case (`mh` instead of `MH`) or the full name instead of the code (`Maharashtra` instead of `MH`). Same underlying state, different string. **Tests:** any segment-level groupby on `ip_state` in EDA (LLD §4.2) will silently fragment a state into multiple bars unless normalized first.
3. **§3.1.3 — Empty-string `device_id`:** 60 rows (0.05%) have `device_id = ""` instead of a real ID or a proper null, simulating a client-side logging failure. **Tests:** `distinct_devices_30d` (LLD §4.3) must treat `""` as "no device," not as a valid distinct device — otherwise it silently undercounts the true device count for affected customers.
4. **§3.1.4 — Non-positive `amount`:** 8 rows have `amount` ≤ 0 (5 rows at exactly 0.0, 3 rows negative), simulating a refund-adjustment row that leaked into the auth export. **Tests:** `validate_schema` should flag these explicitly (log, don't silently drop) since a negative amount breaks `log1p(amount)` in feature engineering.
5. **§3.1.5 — Out-of-window `created_at`:** 3 rows have a `created_at` outside 2026-01-01–2026-10-31 (2 rows dated in 2099, 1 row dated in 2019), simulating a timestamp field corruption. **Tests:** the temporal split (LLD §4.4) must exclude or explicitly handle these — an unhandled 2099 row would land in "test" and silently distort the test window's date range reporting.
6. **§3.1.6 — Negative `checkout_latency_ms`:** 12 rows have a negative value, simulating a clock-skew bug on checkout instrumentation.
7. **§3.1.7 — Implausible `retry_count`:** 5 rows have `retry_count` between 80 and 140 (typical range is 0–4), simulating a bot-driven auth-hammering burst that should be visually obvious in EDA rather than silently smoothed by a model.

### 3.2 `customers.csv` — 35,000 rows

**Grain:** one row per customer. **Primary key:** `customer_id`, intended unique.

| Column | Dtype | Null count | Value domain |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `customer_id` | string | 0 | unique, except §3.2.4 |
| `account_age_days` | int64 | 0 | 1–2,500, except §3.2.3 |
| `lifetime_orders` | int64 | 0 | ≥ 1 |
| `prior_disputes` | int64 | 0 | ≥ 0, snapshot value — see §3.2.1 |
| `avg_order_value` | float64 | 0 | > 0 |
| `email_domain_type` | category | 0 | `personal` (71%), `corporate` (18%), `disposable` (11%), except §3.2.2 |
| `phone_verified` | bool | 0 | |

#### Injected issues in `customers.csv`

1. **§3.2.1 — Stale `prior_disputes`:** for 40 customers, the snapshot value in this column is **lower** than the number of `disputes.csv` rows actually attributable to them as of the snapshot date — simulating a batch job that updates this column on a lag. This is not a "bug to fix": it is the reason LLD §2.2 requires `prior_disputes` to be time-gated and recomputed from `disputes.csv` directly (LLD §4.3, `prior_disputes_before_this_txn`) rather than trusted at face value. **Tests:** if a feature naively uses `customers.prior_disputes` instead of the trailing recomputation, these 40 customers are the ones that will expose the leak/staleness during a manual audit.
2. **§3.2.2 — Empty `email_domain_type`:** 15 rows have `""` instead of one of the three valid categories, simulating a signup-form field that was optional at one point in the product's history.
3. **§3.2.3 — Negative `account_age_days`:** 6 rows are negative, simulating a timezone-boundary bug in the age calculation at signup.
4. **§3.2.4 — Duplicate `customer_id`:** 10 customer_ids each appear on 2 rows (20 rows total) with differing `avg_order_value`, simulating an unresolved merge of two account records. Unique customer_ids: 34,990 across 35,000 rows.

### 3.3 `merchants.csv` — 60 rows

**Grain:** one row per merchant. **Primary key:** `merchant_id`, unique (no violations — the table is small enough that a broken PK here would be implausible and unhelpful to test against).

| Column | Dtype | Null count | Value domain |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `merchant_id` | string | 0 | unique |
| `category` | category | 0 | `travel`, `gaming`, `edtech`, `d2c`, `ticketing`, `subscription` — 10 merchants each |
| `avg_ticket_size` | float64 | 0 | > 0 |
| `refund_window_days` | int64 | 0 | 0–30, except §3.3.2 |
| `delivery_sla_days` | int64 | 39 | null for all `gaming`/`edtech`/`subscription` merchants by design (structural null), except §3.3.1 |

#### Injected issues in `merchants.csv`

1. **§3.3.1 — `delivery_sla_days` populated for a non-physical category:** 2 `gaming` merchants have a non-null `delivery_sla_days`, contradicting the category-based null rule stated in LLD §2.3. This exists specifically so that feature/validation code cannot safely infer "is this merchant physical-goods" purely from `category` — it must check the field's actual nullness, or in this dataset it will misclassify 2 merchants. **Tests:** any code that branches on `category in ('gaming','edtech','subscription')` to decide whether to expect a `delivery_sla_days` value will be wrong for these 2 rows; code that checks `delivery_sla_days.notna()` directly will be correct.
2. **§3.3.2 — Degenerate `refund_window_days`:** 1 `subscription` merchant has `refund_window_days = 0`, an edge case (not an error) worth a one-line note in `METRICS.md` since it means that merchant's `not_as_described`/`duplicate` disputes can never be attributed to "still within refund window."

### 3.4 `fulfilment.csv` — 66,140 rows

**Grain:** intended one row per payment_id in a physical-goods category (`travel`, `d2c`, `ticketing` — 12,000 + 42,000 + 12,000 = 66,000 transactions). **Foreign key:** `payment_id → transactions.payment_id`, **not enforced** (see §2).

| Column | Dtype | Null count | Value domain |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `payment_id` | string | 0 | see §3.4.3 for the 140 orphan rows |
| `shipped_at` | datetime64 | 3,960 (6%) | null if not yet shipped at snapshot |
| `delivered_at` | datetime64 | 9,240 (14%) | null if not yet delivered, except §3.4.2 |
| `delivery_status` | category | 0 | `delivered` (78%), `in_transit` (14%), `returned` (5%), `lost` (3%) |
| `tracking_available` | bool | 0 | |
| `address_completeness_score` | float64 | 0 | 0.0–1.0, except §3.4.4 |

#### Injected issues in `fulfilment.csv`

1. **§3.4.1 — `delivered_at` earlier than `shipped_at`:** 790 rows (1.2% of the 66,000 valid rows) have `delivered_at < shipped_at`, a logically impossible sequence simulating a courier-side timestamp sync error. **Tests:** any feature or chart that computes delivery duration (`delivered_at - shipped_at`) must guard against a negative result rather than silently accepting it — this is exactly the kind of leakage-adjacent table the LLD flags in §2.4, and a negative duration is a strong signal the row shouldn't be trusted at all.
2. **§3.4.2 — Status/timestamp mismatch:** 330 rows (0.5%) have `delivery_status = 'delivered'` but `delivered_at` is null, simulating a status update that fired without its accompanying timestamp write.
3. **§3.4.3 — Orphan rows:** 140 rows reference a `payment_id` not present in `transactions.csv` at all, simulating an ID that was truncated or mistyped on the logistics partner's side during export. These 140 rows are on top of the 66,000 valid rows (140 + 66,000 = 66,140 total).
4. **§3.4.4 — Out-of-range `address_completeness_score`:** 25 rows have a value outside [0, 1] (e.g., 1.15, −0.20), simulating a scoring service that occasionally returns an unclamped value.

### 3.5 `disputes.csv` — 1,091 rows

**Grain:** intended one row per dispute, `payment_id` intended to appear at most once. **Foreign key:** `payment_id → transactions.payment_id`, **not enforced** (see §2).

| Column | Dtype | Null count | Value domain |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `dispute_id` | string | 0 | unique per row |
| `payment_id` | string | 0 | see §3.5.2 for the 6 duplicate-payment_id rows and §3.5.3 for the 35 orphans |
| `reason_code` | category | 5 | `not_received` (38%), `fraud` (24%), `not_as_described` (19%), `subscription_cancelled` (12%), `duplicate` (7%), except §3.5.4 |
| `raised_at` | datetime64 | 0 | 30–90 days after the matching `created_at`, except §3.5.5 |
| `disputed_amount` | float64 | 0 | usually equals `transactions.amount`, except §3.5.1 |

**The label-defining subset:** 1,050 rows have a valid, unique `payment_id` that exists exactly once in `transactions.csv`. These are the rows that set `is_disputed = 1` in `build_label` (LLD §4.1), giving a base dispute rate of **1,050 / 120,000 = 0.875%** — inside the 0.8–1.0% range the LLD's EDA section (§4.2) expects to confirm.

#### Injected issues in `disputes.csv`

1. **§3.5.1 — `disputed_amount` mismatch:** 40 rows have a `disputed_amount` that differs from the matching transaction's `amount` by more than 15%, simulating a partial dispute or a currency-rounding artifact upstream. This is expected behavior per LLD §2.5 ("occasionally partial") but these 40 rows are the tail end of it — large enough gaps to be worth a one-line note in `METRICS.md` rather than silently averaged away.
2. **§3.5.2 — Duplicate `payment_id`:** 6 payment_ids that are already part of the valid 1,050 appear a second time with a different `dispute_id`, simulating a duplicate filing that wasn't deduplicated upstream. This produces 6 extra rows beyond the 1,050. **Tests:** this is the exact condition the "payment_id appears at most once" note in LLD §2.5 exists to warn about, and the join in `build_label` must decide — and document — whether it keeps the first, the last, or flags-and-drops these 6 pairs.
3. **§3.5.3 — Orphan rows:** 35 rows reference a `payment_id` not present in `transactions.csv`, simulating an ID mismatch against the issuing bank's dispute feed. 1,050 + 6 + 35 = 1,091 total rows.
4. **§3.5.4 — Missing `reason_code`:** 5 rows have a null `reason_code`, simulating a dispute that was raised but not yet categorized by the bank at export time.
5. **§3.5.5 — `raised_at` before `created_at`:** 12 rows have a dispute raised *before* the transaction's own `created_at` timestamp — a logical impossibility simulating a timezone or date-parsing bug upstream. **Tests:** any feature computing "days between transaction and dispute" must guard against a negative value here.

## 4. Generation checklist (exact targets)

| Table | Total rows | Orphan FK rows | Duplicate-key rows | Other injected-issue rows |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `transactions.csv` | 120,000 | — | 24 (12 pairs) | 448 (§3.1.2–§3.1.7 combined, non-overlapping) |
| `customers.csv` | 35,000 | — | 20 (10 pairs) | 51 (§3.2.1–§3.2.3 combined) |
| `merchants.csv` | 60 | — | 0 | 3 |
| `fulfilment.csv` | 66,140 | 140 | — | 1,000 (§3.4.1–§3.4.2, §3.4.4 combined, non-overlapping) |
| `disputes.csv` | 1,091 | 35 | 6 | 40 (§3.5.1) + 5 (§3.5.4) + 12 (§3.5.5) = 57, minus overlap with duplicate/orphan rows where applicable |

Generate with `RANDOM_SEED = 42` (per LLD §1) so the exact rows carrying each issue are reproducible run-to-run — this matters because §3's counts are also the expected values the notebook's validation logging should print, and a mismatch on re-generation is itself a signal something in the seeding broke.

---

## 5. Mapping to notebook validation (cross-reference to LLD §4.1)

| This document's issue | Where it's caught | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| §2 orphan FKs (`fulfilment`, `disputes`) | `validate_schema` | Log count, drop row, assert logged count matches this document |
| §2 clean FKs (`merchant_id`, `customer_id`) | `validate_schema` | Raise `AssertionError` on any violation — none expected |
| §3.1.1, §3.2.4, §3.5.2 duplicate keys | `build_label` (transactions↔disputes) and a dedicated `validate_schema` uniqueness check (customers, transactions) | Raise or explicitly deduplicate with a logged, documented rule — never silently keep both |
| §3.1.4 non-positive `amount` | `validate_schema` | Log and exclude from modelling (cannot take `log1p` of ≤0) |
| §3.1.5 out-of-window `created_at` | `temporal_split` | Log and exclude — these rows would otherwise corrupt the reported train/test date ranges |
| §3.1.2 `ip_state` casing | `build_instant_features` | Normalize (uppercase, map full names to codes) before any groupby |
| §3.1.3 empty `device_id` | `build_trailing_features` | Treat `""` as null, not as a distinct device |
| §3.2.1 stale `prior_disputes` | `build_trailing_features` | Never read `customers.prior_disputes` directly for modelling — always recompute `prior_disputes_before_this_txn` from `disputes.csv` |
| §3.3.1 `delivery_sla_days` on `gaming` | `build_instant_features` | Branch on `delivery_sla_days.notna()`, never on `category` membership |
| §3.4.1 `delivered_at < shipped_at` | any fulfilment-derived feature | Guard, treat as missing rather than a negative duration |
| §3.5.5 `raised_at < created_at` | any dispute-timing feature | Guard, treat as missing rather than a negative duration |

This table is the checklist for `METRICS.md`'s data-quality section — each row here should become one line stating the count found and the handling rule applied, so a reader can verify the notebook's cleaning step actually matches what was promised.
